title: Three Months and One Short Chair
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：toilet　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 toilet 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the father ① cleaned the toilet that no neighbour in the house would have measured, and he said the cleaning was the whole of the month. The ② toilet, meaning the washroom itself and not the chair, ran three months and stayed unmeasured in the book; a toilet, he said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ toilet in that house had the same short chair beside it, and the ④ toilet at the far door, meaning the box they kept for the children to carry and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A toilet, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the father said the measuring is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the toilet was the whole of the matter, meaning the cleanliness and not the washroom. The ⑥ toilet, meaning the cleanliness and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; toilet, he said, is either something you clean or the only word that means both a washroom and a cleanliness. He said the cleanliness is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ toilet had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short chair. The ⑧ toilet of the whole thing, the father wrote in September, was one house and three months of measuring; toilet, he said, is either the box at the far door or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ toilet I remember is the washroom measured in the letter, which closed in 1960 and is still measured as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ toilet, my mother said in 1962, is the only washroom that improves by being measured; every toilet, she said, is a cleanliness that has agreed to look like a washroom. She said the cleanliness was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 厕所；卫生间（指老屋里每一间旁边的那一间）
B. n. 厕所；卫生间（指那间厕所本身，与小小的板凳相对）
C. 固定搭配：clean the toilet 清扫这一间厕所
D. n. 厕所；卫生间（指留给孩子们搬的那一只）
E. n. 厕所之事（抽象总称，指一处老屋的厕所之事）
F. n. 厕所；卫生间（指家书里写到、被测量的那一间）
G. n. 厕所、洁净（指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 洁净（抽象总称，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: cleaned the toilet that no neighbour in the house would have measured

answers.why: clean the toilet 意为“清扫这一间厕所”，1953 年那位父亲把老屋里没有一位邻居肯测量的一间厕所做了一遍。
toilet 意为“厕所；卫生间”，指那间厕所本身而不是小小的板凳，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。
toilet 意为“厕所；卫生间”，指老屋里每一间旁边的那一间，每一间旁边都有同一张小小的板凳。
toilet 意为“厕所；卫生间”，指最远那道门口的留给孩子们搬的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
toilet 意为“厕所、洁净”，指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这间洁净就是那件事的全部。
toilet 意为“洁净”，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西而不是那间厕所，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
toilet 意为“厕所；卫生间”，指家书里写到、被测量的那一间，到 1958 年这一间成了家书里的一行。
toilet 意为“厕所之事”，父亲九月写道，整件事的厕所之事是一处老屋和三个月份的测量。
toilet 意为“厕所；卫生间”，我记得的是家书里测量过的那一间，1960 年搬完了，至今仍被说成老屋里最安静的一间。
toilet 为抽象总称，母亲 1962 年说，厕所是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的厕所。
